_shape: Frameworks-shaped, for harnesses measured on the wire. Rows are written by scripts/measure_harness.py from plan/inventory.yaml and the version the binary reports; cells are derived by cells.py from measurements/wire/<harness>/session.json. Never merged with the framework table.

support_codes.y: yes: the answer to the row's question in every judged run (for a which or how-many row: the value was observed)
support_codes.a: yes in some runs or on some servers, not all
support_codes.n: no, in every judged run; the word in the cell says what happened instead
support_codes.u: not measured; the note says why

cursor_agent.name: Cursor agent CLI
cursor_agent.model: Auto Balance, routed to Claude Opus 5.5, routed to GPT-5.6 Sol, routed to Grok 4.7

cell_notes.h-transport-stdio: every session ran with AGENT_CLI_CREDENTIAL_STORE=memory, a switch read in the bundle's src/utils/credential-store.ts at build 2026.10.12 and not in the docs or --help; it keeps the key out of the keychain, where the CLI's default store persists it at every start
cell_notes.h-transport-streamable-http: every session ran with AGENT_CLI_CREDENTIAL_STORE=memory, a switch read in the bundle's src/utils/credential-store.ts at build 2026.10.12 and not in the docs or --help; it keeps the key out of the keychain, where the CLI's default store persists it at every start
cell_notes.h-lists-tools-at-startup: headless Cursor starts no project MCP server without --approve-mcps: the level-1 default session, run with no switch, opened 0 of 5 fixtures, so every level-1 cell reads the stdio-unattended, http-unattended and slow-start-unattended sessions (--force --approve-mcps) and level 2's default mode runs with --approve-mcps alone, which keeps the tool-call approval at its documented default

kiro_cli.name: Kiro CLI
kiro_cli.unattended: --trust-all-tools; ask treated as deny in headless

cell_notes.h-destructive-blocked-by-default: measured headless (cn -p). Headless cn allows every MCP tool ({tool: "*", permission: "allow"} in src/permissions/defaultPolicies.ts); the TUI asks instead, which this run does not measure.
cell_notes.h-expands-prompt: measured headless (cn -p). Slash commands, and so prompts/get, are handled only in the TUI (src/ui/hooks/useChat.ts); -p passes a slash command to the model as text. The TUI path is not measured here.

cell_notes.h-lists-resources-at-startup: changed from y at 0.99.1. Since 1.2.0 Pi no longer lists resources when a server connects: /mcp and `pi mcp list` show that a server offers resources instead of counting them (CHANGELOG 1.2.0, https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10526). Resources are still reachable through the resource tools (h-reads-resource).
cell_notes.h-startup-timeout: level 1 held the stub's reply 10 s, which matches Pi's documented first-prompt wait ("waits up to 10 seconds", docs/mcp.md "Startup" in the package). Since 0.99.2 that wait covers only servers with `direct` tools; codemode servers connect in the background (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212). With the stub answering at once the turn ended about 1 s in, before any server had answered initialize; at 5 s it ended before util, held 8 s, answered. So Pi no longer blocks the first prompt on a slow codemode server, and lists it once it connects.
cell_notes.h-reads-resource: the Pi resource script in plan/harness_sessions.yaml names the server first (`await describeNamespace('mcp__def')`) before calling `tools.read_mcp_resource`, exactly as docs/mcp.md "Startup" describes: "a codemode script waits for the servers it names (`mcp__<server>`)". Pi's script only. Since 1.2.0 the resource tools are registered only once a server with resources has connected, and the call 0.1 s into the turn without that line fails with "tools.read_mcp_resource does not exist" (0/3 at 1.2.0 with the 0.99.1 script).

cell_notes.h-tools-offered-to-model: measured headless in default approval mode. Non-interactive Gemini CLI withholds any tool that would ask, so no MCP tool reaches the model (https://geminicli.com/docs/reference/policy-engine); with --approval-mode yolo all 46 that reached the registry are offered, which is every fixture tool but util's unfetched pages (level2-*-read_only-unattended-*/model.jsonl). Interactive mode asks instead of withholding, which this run does not measure.
cell_notes.h-destructive-blocked-by-default: measured headless in default approval mode, where the tool is withheld from the model rather than held at a prompt (https://geminicli.com/docs/reference/policy-engine). Interactive mode prompts, which this run does not measure.
cell_notes.h-read-only-runs-without-prompt: measured headless in default approval mode, where search_records is withheld from the model despite readOnlyHint (https://geminicli.com/docs/reference/policy-engine). Interactive mode prompts, which this run does not measure.

lifecycle.note: Google is moving Gemini CLI users to Antigravity CLI; since June 18, 2026 Gemini CLI serves Code Assist Standard and Enterprise users.

opencode.name: OpenCode
opencode.mcp_config: opencode.json mcp (write the file; mcp add is interactive)

cell_notes.h-expands-prompt: prompts/get is issued, but with the literal template placeholders {"status": "$1", "tone": "$2"} instead of the user's arguments, which OpenCode substitutes after the server returns (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/33564). A server that branches on an argument sees $1; still so at 1.19.0 although the issue was closed on 2026-10-01.

goose.name: Goose
goose.install: brew install goose (or the install script)

cell_notes.h-answers-elicitation: measured headless (goose run). With no interactive terminal Goose cancels the elicitation and exits: session.json stderr_tail of the level2-2025-11-25-elicit sessions reads "Error: Elicitation requested but no interactive terminal is available to collect user input" (https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/issues/11194). Interactive Goose supports form-mode elicitation (https://goose-docs.ai/docs/guides/mcp-elicitation), which this run does not measure.
cell_notes.h-answers-sampling: correct for the measured release, 1.52.0. Sampling support was removed on Goose main in https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/pull/12193 (merged 2026-09-22), so this cell is expected to change with the first release after it; re-measure then.

cell_notes.h-startup-timeout: measured with Codex's default mcp_optional_startup_grace_ms, 1000 ms: a server that has not answered by then is left out of the first tool catalog (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference). Level 2 sets 30000 and util's tools are then offered (level2-*-slow-*/model.jsonl).
cell_notes.h-follows-pagination: 0.159.2 stopped after the first tools/list page; 0.162.0 started following nextCursor in legacy protocol mode (openai/codex#50035), so this cell and h-tool-count-limit moved with the 0.162.1 re-measure (level1-*-stdio/util.jsonl seq 6, 9, 11).
cell_notes.h-lists-resources-at-startup: Codex lists resources only when the model calls its built-in list_mcp_resources or list_mcp_resource_templates tool; read_mcp_resource reads a URI without a prior list (level2-*-resource-*/def.jsonl: resources/read with no resources/list).
cell_notes.h-tools-offered-to-model: the 4 changed schemas lose JSON Schema keywords: format, minimum, maximum and default are dropped, and oneOf of const values becomes enum (def/search_records, def/explain_topic, def/deliver_payload, util/cancellable_wait; level2-*/model.jsonl fixture_tools against def.jsonl tools/list).
cell_notes.h-calls-read-only-tool: the call is sent and answered, but Codex 0.162.1 still fails the result with "Unexpected response type" because search_records returns a text block with audience and priority annotations; any result carrying that block fails the same way (res/annotated_content, res/mixed_content), and unannotated blocks of every type pass (level2-*-read_only-*/harness.jsonl).
cell_notes.h-destructive-blocked-by-default: measured headless: codex exec's default approval policy is never, so a call that needs approval fails with "MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never" instead of prompting. Interactive Codex prompts, which this run does not measure (level2-*-destructive-*/harness.jsonl).

measured headless (crush run), which approves every permission request of its own session (RunNonInteractive calls AutoApproveSession, https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/v0.98.1/internal/app/app.go) and has no flag to ask instead; --yolo exists only on the root command. The TUI asks for permission, which this run does not measure.
cell_notes.h-expands-prompt: measured headless (crush run). MCP prompts are commands in Crush's TUI (https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/v0.98.1/internal/commands/commands.go); crush run sends its text to the model as is, so prompts/get is never reached. The TUI path is not measured here.
cell_notes.h-relist-next-turn: measured headless (crush run), which builds its tool palette once per run ("Non-interactive runs get a single shot at the tool palette", https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/v0.98.1/internal/agent/coordinator.go). The TUI refreshes tools on list_changed, which this run does not measure.
cell_notes.h-tools-offered-to-model: the 41 changed schemas differ only by an added "required": [] where the server omitted required: Crush rebuilds each input schema from properties and required alone (Tool.Info, https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/v0.98.1/internal/agent/tools/mcp-tools.go), so any other top-level keyword would be dropped (level1-*-stdio/model.jsonl fixture_tools against tools/list).

cell_notes.h-reacts-to-list-changed: the headless process exits 0.25 to 0.52 s after fixture ntf sends notifications/tools/list_changed, so a re-list deferred past that could not be seen. In that window no second tools/list is sent, 6/6 (level2-*-relist-*/ntf.jsonl, notification at seq 14, capture end at seq 16).
cell_notes.h-tools-offered-to-model: Qwen Code defers MCP tools by default (tools.toolSearch.enabled, default true): none is declared to the model, which looks one up with the built-in tool_search ("select:<name>") and invokes it through tool_call (level1-*-stdio/model.jsonl request 1 offers both and no fixture tool). Every level-2 call in this capture goes through that pair.
cell_notes.h-destructive-blocked-by-default: measured headless with --approval-mode default, pinned because the flagless start mode is auto, whose LLM classifier a stub cannot answer (the exception to "default means shipped default" in plan/harness_sessions.yaml). Headless, a call that needs approval is declined with "non-interactive mode cannot prompt for confirmation" and listed in permission_denials. Interactive mode prompts, which this run does not measure (level2-*-destructive-[123]/harness.jsonl).
cell_notes.h-read-only-runs-without-prompt: measured headless with --approval-mode default (pinned as for h-destructive-blocked-by-default). search_records carries readOnlyHint: true and is declined exactly like delete_account (level2-*-read_only-[123]/harness.jsonl permission_denied).
cell_notes.h-reads-resource: the built-in read_mcp_resource needs approval in default mode and is declined headless (level2-*-resource-*/harness.jsonl permission_denied); no resources/read reaches def. Qwen Code's documented user-side route, @server:uri in the prompt, is not exercised by this session.
cell_notes.h-relist-next-turn: after add_tool fires list_changed, the model's next tool_search for SENTINEL_ADDED_TOOL returns "1 missing" and tool_call refuses it as not registered (level2-*-relist-*/harness.jsonl), 6/6.
cell_notes.h-lists-resources-at-startup: resources/list is sent at startup in 6/6 level-1 sessions; resources/templates/list is sent in none (level1-*/def.jsonl).
cell_notes.h-answers-elicitation: the client declares no elicitation capability and answers the fixture's elicitation/create with -32601 Method not found (level2-*-elicit-*/cf.jsonl seq 15), 6/6.
cell_notes.h-answers-sampling: the client declares no sampling capability and answers the fixture's sampling/createMessage with -32601 Method not found (level2-*-sampling-*/cf.jsonl seq 15), 6/6.

kilo.name: Kilo CLI
kilo.mcp_config: kilo.jsonc mcp or kilo mcp add

cell_notes.h-lists-prompts-at-startup: Kilo fetches prompts on demand, not at startup: the prompt session shows prompts/list on def just before prompts/get, when kilo run --command builds its command list (level2-*-prompt-*/def.jsonl). n means not at startup, not unsupported.
cell_notes.h-lists-resources-at-startup: Kilo lists no resources at startup; its built-in list_mcp_resources and read_mcp_resource tools fetch them when the model calls them (https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/mcp/using-in-kilo-code). read_mcp_resource reads a URI without a prior list (level2-*-resource-*/def.jsonl).
cell_notes.h-tools-offered-to-model: the schema change only adds keys: every input schema gains "additionalProperties": false, and "properties": {} where it has none. Descriptions are unchanged, and no annotation reaches the model (level1-*-stdio/model.jsonl).
cell_notes.h-destructive-blocked-by-default: measured headless (kilo run without --auto). Kilo's docs say a non-interactive run auto-rejects any permission request (https://kilo.ai/docs/code-with-ai/platforms/cli), but no request was raised: delete_account (destructiveHint: true) reached the server with no permission event in 6/6 runs (level2-*-destructive-[123]/harness.jsonl). The approval prompt the MCP docs describe (https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/mcp/using-in-kilo-code) is not raised for MCP tools under kilo run's default config.
cell_notes.h-expands-prompt: prompts/get is issued, but with the literal template placeholders {"status": "$1", "tone": "$2"} instead of the user's arguments in 6/6 runs, the behaviour Kilo inherits from OpenCode (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/33564). A server that branches on an argument sees $1.
cell_notes.h-answers-elicitation: Kilo declares only roots and answers elicitation/create with -32601 Method not found on both lines; it requests 2025-11-25 on both, so MRTR is not exercised (level2-*-elicit-*/cf.jsonl).
cell_notes.h-answers-sampling: Kilo declares only roots and answers sampling/createMessage with -32601 Method not found on both lines; it requests 2025-11-25 on both, so MRTR is not exercised (level2-*-sampling-*/cf.jsonl).
cell_notes.h-tolerates-progress: the five progress notifications arrive and the result reaches the model; about 0.1 s after the response Kilo sends notifications/cancelled for the answered request (reason "AbortError: The operation was aborted.") in 6/6 runs (level2-*-slow-*/util.jsonl). The cancel is harmless here.

cell_notes.h-destructive-blocked-by-default: measured headless (openhands --headless). "Headless mode always runs in always-approve mode" and that cannot be changed (https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/cli/headless), so default and unattended are the same state; security_risk HIGH changes nothing there. The interactive CLI confirms actions, which this run does not measure.
cell_notes.h-tools-offered-to-model: every schema gains a required security_risk and a summary property, readOnlyHint tools included: with mcp 2.2.0 the SDK reads annotations back as defaults (openhands/sdk/mcp/tool.py MCPToolDefinition.create). The schemas also lose enum, format, minimum, maximum and default, nested object properties (def/create_report config) and anyOf/oneOf (def/deliver_payload destination) (level1-*-stdio/model.jsonl fixture_tools against def.jsonl tools/list).
cell_notes.h-answers-elicitation: OpenHands declares the elicitation capability and then answers elicitation/create with -32603 "Elicitation not supported" (level2-2025-11-25-elicit-*/cf.jsonl); that text is the mcp library's default callback (mcp/client/session.py), so no handler stands behind the declared capability.
cell_notes.h-answers-sampling: OpenHands declares the sampling capability and then answers sampling/createMessage with -32603 "Sampling not supported" (level2-2025-11-25-sampling-*/cf.jsonl); that text is the mcp library's default callback (mcp/client/session.py), so no handler stands behind the declared capability.

cell_notes.h-lists-prompts-at-startup: no prompts/list in 6/6 level-1 sessions (level1-*/def.jsonl). "MCP prompt templates are unsupported" (dsh-mcp-client README, https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/dsh-v0.2.0-rc.2/packages/mcp/mcp-client).
cell_notes.h-lists-resources-at-startup: no resources/list or resources/templates/list in 6/6 level-1 sessions (level1-*/res.jsonl). Resources are read on demand through the shipped mcp-resources tools the model calls (dsh-mcp-client README, "Resources are read on demand"); that path needs a model-driven call, which level 2 would measure and does not here.
cell_notes.h-reacts-to-list-changed: u because ntf fires notifications/tools/list_changed only after a tool call, and level 1 makes none. On 2026-07-28 dsh does open subscriptions/listen on ntf and gets notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged (level1-2026-07-28-*/ntf.jsonl), and its docs say a list change queues a re-sync (dsh-mcp-client README, "Lifecycle and sync"); neither is a measured reaction.

cell_notes.h-lists-prompts-at-startup: Roo never sends prompts/list, at startup or later, in any of the 72 sessions. McpHub fetches only tools, resources and resource templates (fetchToolsList, fetchResourcesList and fetchResourceTemplatesList in src/services/mcp/McpHub.ts); the SDK's listPrompts is never called (level1-*/def.jsonl).
cell_notes.h-follows-pagination: Roo sends one tools/list with no cursor and ignores nextCursor (fetchToolsList), so util's first page of 20 is all the model sees and 40 of its 60 tools are never offered (level1-*/util.jsonl).
cell_notes.h-reacts-to-list-changed: ntf sends notifications/tools/list_changed after add_tool, and Roo registers no handler for it: ntf is listed once, at startup, in 6/6 runs (level2-*-relist-*/ntf.jsonl).
cell_notes.h-tools-offered-to-model: 46/46 listed tools are offered as mcp--<server>--<tool> with descriptions unchanged; every schema gains "additionalProperties": false, format is dropped inside anyOf (deliver_payload's "format": "uri"), and no annotation reaches the model (level2-*-read_only-unattended-*/model.jsonl).
cell_notes.h-read-only-runs-without-prompt: measured headless (roo -p, no --require-approval). Roo auto-approves an MCP tool only if it is in its server's alwaysAllow list (https://docs.roocode.com/features/mcp/using-mcp-in-roo), whatever its annotations, so read-only search_records is held like delete_account. In print mode the CLI never answers the ask, and the run hangs until it is killed at 300 s, in 6/6 runs (level2-*-read_only-[123]/harness.jsonl).
cell_notes.h-expands-prompt: Roo has no MCP prompt surface: it never lists prompts and no command or tool expands one, so no prompts/get reached def in 6/6 runs (level2-*-prompt-*/def.jsonl).
cell_notes.h-answers-elicitation: Roo declares no client capabilities and answers elicitation/create with -32601 Method not found on both lines; it requests 2025-03-26 on both (level2-*-elicit-*/cf.jsonl).
cell_notes.h-answers-sampling: Roo declares no client capabilities and answers sampling/createMessage with -32601 Method not found on both lines (level2-*-sampling-*/cf.jsonl).
cell_notes.h-relist-next-turn: Roo never re-lists ntf after notifications/tools/list_changed, so SENTINEL_ADDED_TOOL is never offered in 6/6 runs; the session then runs to its 300 s timeout (level2-*-relist-*/model.jsonl).

lifecycle.note: Roo Code was shut down on May 15, 2026 and its repository is archived. This measurement is of its last CLI release.
